title: An RDMA-First Object Storage System with SmartNIC Offload
problem: AI training workloads generate fine-grain I/O that saturates host-mediated TCP paths; kernel involvement and context switches limit storage throughput for GPU-centric pipelines.
motivation: LLM training requires high-throughput, low-latency I/O; kernel bypass (RDMA) proven efficient; offloading client logic to Smart-NIC reduces host overhead and enables security services.
method: ROS2 architecture: RDMA-first DAOS client offloaded to NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPU. Separates control plane (gRPC, lightweight) from data plane (RDMA/UCX, high-throughput). Keeps server-side DAOS I/O engine unchanged. Supports multi-tenant isolation and inline encryption on SmartNIC.
key_novelty: First practical DAOS/SmartNIC integration with RDMA offload achieving host-comparable performance; demonstrates DPU viability for object storage in AI workloads.
contributions: ROS2 RDMA-first object storage design with SmartNIC offload
BlueField-3 DAOS client offloading achieving comparable host performance
Control/data plane separation enabling efficient scaling
Multi-tenant isolation and inline services on DPU
limitations: Limited to FIO/DFS microbenchmarks; real LLM training evaluation not provided; GPU-direct placement left future work; SmartNIC cost/availability not discussed.
primary_theme: SmartNIC-offloaded object storage for AI training
